evidence.detail: is_in_current_run() returns True for any league deck with <5 matches, not retired, and in an active competition — so a formerly 5-0 deck with one match deleted becomes active again

guarantee_at_most_one_or_retire() retires decks[0] and keeps decks[1]; but decks are sorted alphabetically (person+name), not by created_date, so the newer deck may be retired instead of the older one
active_decks() sorts by 'person.ljust(100)+name' — no date-based ordering, so the 'wrong' deck can end up as decks[0] and be retired
No 'finalized' or 'completed' column exists in deck table — the proper fix proposed in comments has not been implemented

triage.notes: A no-migration partial fix (sort active_decks by created_date and retire the oldest in guarantee_at_most_one_or_retire) is possible, but bakert's comments note it conflicts with the 'never-retired-a-deck' achievement. The proper fix (a 'finalized' column set when the fifth match is reported) requires a migration and a product decision.
